name: LSASS Credential Dump Detection via Sysmon Event 10
command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\Dump\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 10} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List
description: Detect credential dumping from LSASS memory using Sysmon Event ID 10 (ProcessAccess). Tools like Mimikatz open a handle to lsass.exe with specific access rights — Sysmon captures this handle request and records the calling process, enabling detection.
source: CDSA Module 03: Windows Event Logs & Finding Evil
notes:
Sysmon Event ID 10 (ProcessAccess) key fields:
  SourceImage        → process that opened the handle (attacker's process)
  TargetImage        → target process being accessed (lsass.exe)
  GrantedAccess      → access rights mask granted (key for detection)
  CallTrace          → stack trace of the API call chain

Malicious GrantedAccess values for lsass.exe:
  0x1010  → PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
  0x1410  → PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | ...
  0x1fffff → PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS (loud — full access requested)
  → Any access to lsass.exe from a non-system process is suspicious

Mimikatz commands (attack reference):
  privilege::debug           → enable SeDebugPrivilege (required for lsass access)
  sekurlsa::logonpasswords   → dump plaintext credentials and hashes from LSASS memory

CallTrace analysis:
  Legitimate lsass access (e.g. AV): callstack shows signed system DLLs
  Malicious access (Mimikatz): callstack may show unknown/unsigned modules
  → Look for UNKNOWN regions in CallTrace (indicates reflective injection)

Lab analysis path: C:\Logs\Dump\
  → Contains sysmon.evtx with LSASS dump evidence
  → Look for Event 10 where TargetImage = C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe

Additional detections:
  Security Event 4656 → Handle request to an object (if object access auditing enabled)
  Security Event 4663 → Access attempt to LSASS process object
  Windows Defender → 'Credential Theft' alert triggered by Mimikatz signatures

Filtering lsass access via XPath:
  Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' -FilterXPath
    "*[System[EventID=10] and EventData[Data[@Name='TargetImage']='C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe']]"

examples.label: Read Dump lab evtx — all Event 10 (ProcessAccess) events
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\Dump\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 10} | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List

examples.label: Live detection — filter Sysmon Event 10 where target is lsass.exe
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' -FilterXPath "*[System[EventID=10] and EventData[Data[@Name='TargetImage']='C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe']]" | Select-Object TimeCreated, Message | Format-List

examples.label: Parse Event 10 XML — extract SourceImage, TargetImage, GrantedAccess
examples.command: Get-WinEvent -Path 'C:\Logs\Dump\sysmon.evtx' | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 10} | ForEach-Object { $xml=[xml]$_.ToXml(); $data=$xml.Event.EventData.Data; [PSCustomObject]@{Time=$_.TimeCreated; Source=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'SourceImage'}).'#text'; Target=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'TargetImage'}).'#text'; Access=($data|?{$_.Name -eq 'GrantedAccess'}).'#text'} } | Format-Table -AutoSize
